top_choice_rationale: P001, Mircea Cărtărescu alone, is the only writer on the slate and the proposal I judge on literary grounds. His voice is recognisable at the level of the sentence and of the whole book. Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known, build the body, memory and dream into one large imaginative architecture, and Solenoid is received as a different construction from the earlier trilogy, which counts against mere repetition. The poetry and shorter prose attach to the same project, so a whole-oeuvre citation is defensible. I would keep the citation on form and imagination, without national or 'European tradition' framing. Caveats: I cannot assess the Romanian rhythm, long-sentence control or wordplay, and translation coverage of the poetry, early work and essays is thinner than for the novels. My judgment rests on public knowledge and reception, not on independent reading. The unanimous round-2 support is not merit evidence for me. The open reading of the will's 'idealistic tendency' remains an interpretation, and I do not think the inward and disturbing character of the work disqualifies it. P000 ranks below because the case, though shaped by those caveats, is serious enough to prefer an award to none.
